providers.detectionDescription: Set OPENROUTER_API_KEY environment variable or add [openrouter].api_key to config.toml.
providers.envNote: Restart Agents Usage Bar to apply environment variable changes.
providers.tomlNote: Save the file — changes apply on next poll.

providers.detectionDescription: Run Claude Code (ccs) at least once to create ~/.claude/projects/ transcript files, or sign in via Claude CLI to create ~/.claude/.credentials.json.
providers.envSnippet: # Claude is detected automatically from ~/.claude/ — no manual key needed.
providers.envNote: Claude Code creates credential files automatically when you log in.
providers.tomlSnippet: # No TOML config needed for Claude — detected from ~/.claude/ automatically.
providers.tomlNote: Run `claude login` or use Claude Code to create the required files.

providers.detectionDescription: Run OpenAI Codex CLI at least once to create ~/.codex/sessions/ files, or sign in to create ~/.codex/auth.json.
providers.envSnippet: # Codex is detected automatically from ~/.codex/ — no manual key needed.
providers.envNote: Codex CLI creates credential files automatically when you log in.
providers.tomlSnippet: # No TOML config needed for Codex — detected from ~/.codex/ automatically.
providers.tomlNote: Run `codex login` to create the required files.

providers.detectionDescription: Run gemini-cli and select 'Login with Google' (oauth-personal) to create ~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json and set selectedAuthType in ~/.gemini/settings.json.
providers.envSnippet: # Gemini is detected automatically from ~/.gemini/ — no manual key needed.
providers.envNote: Gemini CLI creates credential files automatically when you log in.
providers.tomlSnippet: # No TOML config needed for Gemini — detected from ~/.gemini/ automatically.
providers.tomlNote: Run `gemini login` and select the oauth-personal auth method.

providers.detectionDescription: Run `grok login` to create ~/.grok/auth.json, or set XAI_API_KEY. Sessions under ~/.grok/sessions also count as detected.
providers.envSnippet:
# Optional fallback when no grok login session is stored.
export XAI_API_KEY=<your-xai-key>
providers.envNote: Restart Agents Usage Bar to apply environment variable changes. Prefer `grok login` so the app can read ~/.grok/auth.json.
providers.tomlSnippet:
# No API key in TOML — Grok reads ~/.grok/auth.json automatically.
[grok]
enabled = true
providers.tomlNote: Save the file — enable/disable applies on next app restart.

providers.detectionDescription: Start Ollama — detected via HTTP probe on localhost:11434.
providers.envNote: Ollama is detected when running on its default port (11434). No configuration needed.
providers.tomlSnippet: # No TOML config needed — Ollama detected automatically on port 11434.
providers.tomlNote: Pull a model first: ollama pull llama3

providers.detectionDescription: Start LM Studio server — detected via HTTP probe on localhost:1234 (default port).
providers.envSnippet: # Start LM Studio server from the LM Studio app UI.
providers.envNote: LM Studio is detected when its server is running. Default port is 1234.
providers.tomlSnippet:
[lmstudio]
port = 1234  # change if you use a custom port
providers.tomlNote: Save the file — port change applies on next app restart.

providers.detectionDescription: Configure the port in config.toml, then start llama-server — detected via HTTP probe on that port.
providers.envNote: llama.cpp requires a port in config.toml first — it is never auto-scanned.
providers.tomlSnippet:
[llamacpp]
port = 8080  # replace with your llama-server port
providers.tomlNote: Save the file — changes apply on next app restart.
